Smaller bundles and a faster first call. The API, normalized output, and error messages are unchanged.

## Size

| import | 1.0.0 min | 1.0.1 min | 1.0.0 gzip | 1.0.1 gzip |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `@adraffy/ens-normalize.ts` | 22,697 | 22,031 | 16,403 | 16,116 |
| `@adraffy/ens-normalize.ts/xnf` | 17,095 | 16,705 | 12,141 | 11,971 |
| `@adraffy/ens-normalize.ts/full` | 25,074 | 24,554 | 17,655 | 17,394 |

Bytes, minified ESM. Core is 42% smaller than ens-normalize.js 1.11.1 (38.3 KB).

- **Property renaming:** terser now shortens internal property names in every bundle.
- **Smaller data:** the NF blob goes from 4,730 to 4,461 chars and the ENS blob from 10,494 to 10,297. Combining class ranks are stored as indices into the CM set, mapped codepoints use gaps that skip valid ones, mapped outputs are predicted from the previous entry, and whole-script confusables name their whole by recency rank.

## Speed

The first call, which decodes the data, is about 2.6x faster:

| first call (import + `ensNormalize`) | Bun | Node |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1.0.0 `index.js` | 51.9 ms | 83.2 ms |
| 1.0.1 `index.js` | 20.0 ms | 31.0 ms |
| 1.0.0 `xnf.js` | 42.6 ms | 74.6 ms |
| 1.0.1 `xnf.js` | 17.3 ms | 27.1 ms |
| ens-normalize.js 1.11.1 | 59.8 ms | 89.4 ms |

Medians of 41 fresh processes, Bun 1.4.4 and Node 26.13. Retained heap after init under Node drops from 23.1 MB to 14.5 MB.

- The decoder keeps its probabilities in a typed array.
- Groups share the large codepoint sets (Han is used by four groups) instead of copying them.
- Work that only some names need is deferred: the whole-script confusable table is built by the first label that isn't ASCII (about 7 ms under Bun, 9 ms under Node), and whether a codepoint belongs to a single group is worked out the first time it's checked.

Normalizing speed after the first call is unchanged.

## Other changes

- In `full`, `nfc()` and `nfd()` now load the ENS data on first use too, because the NF tables are stored relative to it.
- `bun run test:labels` (development only) compares the core API against ens-normalize.js on all 3,422,100 labels in [adraffy/ens-labels](https://github.com/adraffy/ens-labels).

## Verification

- All 38,614 ENSIP-15 validation tests and Unicode's NormalizationTest pass in every bundle (ESM and CJS).
- All 3,422,100 labels in adraffy/ens-labels give the same output and error messages as ens-normalize.js, for the source and all six bundles.
- Browser tests: https://adraffy.github.io/ens-normalize.ts/
